# agent-build-tools

GitHub-Issues-native ticketing toolkit for agent-driven software builds. A
ticket IS a GitHub Issue — open = to-do, closed = done, no shadow task files.
The toolkit owns selection, context assembly, verification, and the whole
git/PR ceremony so the executing model only writes code.

Extracted from the [Niffler](https://github.com/darthzen/niffler) build after
it ran that project's plan end to end; generalized so any repo can adopt it by
dropping in one config file. Current consumers: Niffler (SwiftUI app) and
[nemoclaw-ops-agent](https://github.com/darthzen/nemoclaw-ops-agent)
(Kubernetes/agent infrastructure) — two very different stacks, same workflow.

## Model

- **Serial flow:** `new` → `next` → `start` → `show` → implement → `finish`
  (verify, branch, commit, push, PR, squash-merge, close issue).
- **Parallel flow (one orchestrator, N worker worktrees):** `capacity` →
  `batch` → `worktree-add` → workers `submit` → orchestrator `land`
  (serialized squash-merge behind a file lock, rebase-and-retry on conflict).
- **`doctor [--fix]`** reconciles issues ↔ commits ↔ board ↔ branches.

## Adopting in a repo

1. Add this repo as a submodule (or copy the script):
   `git submodule add https://github.com/darthzen/agent-build-tools build-plan/tools`
2. `cp build-plan/tools/config.example.yaml build-plan/config.yaml` and edit —
   the `tooling:` section carries everything project-specific (runnable
   acceptance commands, per-command cwd, test-path template, optional extra
   build gate, §-citation doc).
3. Create tickets with
   `python3 build-plan/tools/agent-tools.py new "Title" --milestone M0 --area infra ...`
   — never hand-write issue bodies; the tooling parses what it emits.

Requires: `gh` (authenticated), `git`, Python 3 with PyYAML.

## Ticket format

Issue title `T-012 · Do the thing`; body header carries
`**Milestone:** … | **Assignee:** agent|human | **Depends on:** T-…` and a
`**Files** — create: […]; modify: […]` line, then `## Context / ## Steps /
## Acceptance`. Acceptance bullets containing backtick-quoted runnable
commands are executed by `verify`/`finish`; anything else is a human checklist.

Conventions that make agent execution safe: tickets declare their files and
agents may touch nothing else; `human`-labeled tickets are dependencies, never
picked up; acceptance must pass before any commit; the tooling owns git.

## Session provenance (Entire)

`finish` and `land` merge with `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`. GitHub
builds a **new** commit server-side and deletes the branch, so any
[Entire](https://entire.io) checkpoint that the post-commit hook attached to the
local task-branch commit is orphaned — it points at a SHA that never reaches
`main`, and the agent session that wrote the code loses its link to the merged
work.

Enable the opt-in `entire:` block in `config.yaml` and the toolkit re-anchors the
session onto the squash commit after the merge:

```yaml
entire:
  enabled: true
  agent: claude-code   # passed to `entire session attach --agent`
  amend: false         # link via the metadata ref only — no history rewrite on main
```

- **Serial (`finish`):** captures the active session before the git ceremony and
  runs `entire session attach <sid>` once `main` is updated.
- **Parallel (`submit` → `land`):** `submit` records the worker's session id as an
  `Entire-Session:` trailer in the PR body; `land` reads it back and re-anchors
  after the merge, **before** tearing down the worktree (and its session store).

With `amend: false` the attach links through Entire's metadata ref and never
rewrites or force-pushes `main`. The whole path is best-effort — an Entire
failure prints a note but never blocks a land. Omit the block entirely (the
default) and the toolkit stays Entire-unaware. Requires the `entire` CLI on PATH
and `entire enable` already run in the target repo.
=====ISSUE_TEMPLATE=====
# Agent-ready issue template

Every ticket follows this shape. It exists so deepseek-coder-v2:16b never has to infer or improvise. If a section can't be filled concretely, the task is too big — split it.

Each issue body (rendered from `tasks.yaml`) contains:

```markdown
## Context
One or two sentences: what this delivers and why. Link the spec section, e.g. "Schema §4 Item core".

## Dependencies
- T-0xx (must be closed first)
- none

## Files
Create:
- `Sources/NifflerCore/Models/Item.swift`
Modify:
- (exact paths, or "none")
Do NOT touch anything else.

## Steps
1. Concrete, ordered instructions. Name types, properties, and signatures explicitly.
2. ...

## Acceptance
Runnable checks. The task is done only when all pass.
- [ ] `swift build` succeeds
- [ ] `swift test --filter ItemTests` passes
- [ ] Item has properties: id, collectionId, name, maker, model, modelYear?, manufactureYear?, isReissue, ...

## Out of scope / guardrails
- Don't add persistence here (that's T-0xx).
- No new dependencies.

## Definition of done
Project builds, all acceptance checks pass, change is limited to the listed files, committed as `[T-0xx] <title>` with `Closes #<n>`.
```

## Authoring rules

- **One concern per ticket** — roughly one file or one tightly-scoped change. If acceptance needs more than ~4 checks, split.
- **Name everything** — exact type names, property names, function signatures, file paths. No "etc.", no "and so on".
- **Acceptance must be executable** — a build command and/or a named test. Prefer a test the agent can run with `swift test --filter <Name>`.
- **State the guardrails** — what NOT to touch, so an autonomous run can't sprawl.
- **Mark `assignee`** — `agent` for pure Swift/test/code work; `human` for Xcode project, signing, secrets, App Store, or anything needing a GUI or credentials.
- **Declare `depends_on`** — so the runner only ever picks unblocked work.
=====CONFIG=====
# Copy to <your-repo>/build-plan/config.yaml and adjust.
# Tickets are GitHub Issues (open = to-do, closed = done); this file holds
# project-wide config only, never ticket data.
project:
  name: MyProject
  repo: "owner/repo"
  project_number: 1        # GitHub Project (v2) board number; omit to skip boards
  build_through: M5        # highest milestone agents may build ($BUILD_THROUGH overrides)
  board_status: false      # true → push Status via API (costs GraphQL quota)
projects: {}               # optional milestone → project_number overrides, e.g. {M13: 2}

# Project-type tooling. Omitting this section preserves the original
# swift-project defaults, so pre-extraction configs work unchanged.
tooling:
  # Acceptance commands must start with one of these to be executed by verify/finish:
  runnable: [bash, sh, python, python3, kubectl, kubeconform, helm, pytest, shellcheck, cd]
  # Per-command working directory (first match wins; default repo root):
  cwd_rules:
    - {command: swift, dir: Packages/MyCore}
  # Where `--filter <Name>` test files live (auto-staged by finish/submit):
  test_path_template: "Packages/MyCore/Tests/MyCoreTests/{name}.swift"
  # Extra build gate for tickets touching these paths/labels (omit to disable):
  app_build:
    paths: ["App/", "AppTests/"]
    labels: ["area:ui"]
    command: "xcodebuild -scheme App -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' build -quiet"
  # Doc searched for §N citations by `show`:
  schema_doc: docs/Data-Model-Schema.md
  # Acceptance line for `new` when no body is given:
  default_acceptance: "python3 -m pytest -q"

# Session provenance (Entire). Omit this block entirely to keep the toolkit
# Entire-unaware (the default). When enabled, finish/land run
# `entire session attach` after the squash-merge to re-anchor the farming
# session onto the surviving squash commit — otherwise `gh pr merge --squash`
# orphans the checkpoint the post-commit hook left on the deleted task branch.
entire:
  enabled: false         # true → re-anchor sessions after each finish/land
  agent: claude-code     # agent name passed to `entire session attach --agent`
  amend: false           # false → link via Entire's metadata ref only (no rewrite,
                         #   safe on an already-pushed main). true → also amend the
                         #   squash commit with the trailer (rewrites HEAD; only for
                         #   local-only flows where main isn't pushed yet).

# Env knobs (all optional): AGENT_BOARD, AGENT_MAX_WORKERS, AGENT_BUILD_RAM_GB,
# AGENT_RAM_RESERVE_GB, AGENT_APP_BUILD_CMD, BUILD_THROUGH, PROJECT_NUMBER.
# Legacy NIFFLER_* names are honored as fallbacks.

server over the SUSE NeuVector container security platform, written to be
implemented correctly by a 30B-class coding model.

## How to drive `qwen3-coder:30b` through it

The single biggest failure mode for a 30B model on a project this size is context
exhaustion followed by invention. The phase structure exists to prevent that: each
phase is small enough to hold, and each ends in a gate the model cannot argue with.

### Session 0 — orientation

```
Read SPEC.md in full. Then read phases/PHASE-0-scaffold.md and do only that
phase. Report the two gate outcomes. Do not read any other phase file.
```

### Sessions 1-11 — one phase per session

Start a **fresh context** for each phase. The prompt is the same shape every time:

```
You are implementing the NeuVector MCP server, phase N.

Read, in this order:
  1. SPEC.md sections 0 (rules), <the sections that phase names>
  2. phases/PHASE-N-<name>.md
  3. only the tools/PART-X.md sections that phase names

Then implement the phase. Run its gate command. Report:
  - the exact tool count from `make spec`
  - the `make verify` result
  - any BLOCKED item you hit

Do not read other phase files. Do not start phase N+1.
```

### When a gate fails

Feed the failure back verbatim and nothing else:

```
`make verify` failed with:
<paste output>

Fix only what this output names. Do not refactor anything that passes.
```

Resist the urge to let the model "improve" passing code. Every rewrite of a
passing module is a new chance to break it.

### If the model reports `BLOCKED`

That is the spec working as designed. `BLOCKED` means the model looked for an
endpoint or a field, did not find it in the appendices, and refused to invent one.
Resolve it yourself — usually by checking a live controller — then hand back the
concrete answer. Do not tell the model to "figure it out".

---

## Why the spec is shaped this way

Six choices do most of the work in getting a 30B model to a correct result.

**A working core, not a description of one.** `reference/` is not pseudocode. It
is 9 modules plus 2 tool modules that were executed in a sandbox: 11 tests pass,
all 9 gate rules pass. Phase 0 copies it. The model therefore starts from working
auth, retry, error classification, the write guard and the audit middleware — the
parts it would most likely get subtly wrong — and only ever writes tools.

**A machine-checkable gate, not a review.** `scripts/verify_spec.py` introspects
the assembled server and enforces 9 rules: naming, description structure,
annotation consistency, toolset tagging, the `confirm` parameter, the endpoint
allowlist, structured output, test coverage, and registration. "Looks right" is
not an outcome the model can claim.

**An endpoint allowlist derived from source.** Appendix A was generated by
parsing `controller/api/apis.yaml` (232 operations) and `controller/rest/rest.go`
(340 registered routes). Gate rule R6 parses the `Calls <METHOD> <path>` line out
of every docstring and checks it against that list. A hallucinated endpoint fails
the build rather than failing in production.

**Phases sized to a context window.** Each phase file is under 200 lines and
names the exact sections to read. The tool contracts are split across four files
so no phase needs more than one.

**Read and write toolsets that never mix.** A toolset is entirely read or
entirely write, so `readOnlyHint` is derivable from the tag and rule R3 can check
it mechanically. `NV_READ_ONLY=true` plus a mutating toolset is a startup error,
not a silent downgrade.

**A confirmation handshake the model cannot skip.** Every mutating tool returns a
plan with a payload-bound token on the first call and only acts on the second.
The test that asserts `route.call_count == 0` on the preview call is the entire
safety model compressed into one line.

---

## Verified, not recalled

Everything below was established in a live sandbox on 2026-07-29, not from memory.

| Claim | How it was established |
|---|---|
| 232 documented operations, 396 schema definitions | parsed `controller/api/apis.yaml` from `neuvector/neuvector@main` |
| 340 registered routes, 112 undocumented | parsed `controller/rest/rest.go` and diffed against the Swagger paths |
| Query conventions (`f_`, `s_`, `start`, `limit`, operator degradation) | read `restParseQuery` in `controller/rest/rest.go` and the constants in `controller/api/apis.go` |
| Auth header precedence and API key format | read `restReq2User` in `controller/rest/auth.go` |
| Error codes 1-55 with their exact strings | extracted from `apis.go` constants joined to the `restErrMessage` table in `rest.go` |
| FastMCP 3.4.5 API surface | installed it and introspected `FastMCP.__init__`, `.tool()`, `.run_http_async()`, `list_tools()`, `Middleware`, `StaticTokenVerifier` |
| The reference core works | ran it: 11 tests pass, `verify_spec.py` reports 9/9 rules clean |
| openSUSE BCI Python 3.13 exists | queried the registry tag list: `3.13` → 3.13.13 |
| All 84 endpoint references in the tool contracts are valid | ran the gate's own R6 matcher over every `Calls` line: 0 violations |

Where the upstream schema does not cover a type, the tool contracts say
`BLOCKED (schema)` and give a defensive projection plus an instruction to confirm
against a live controller. Nothing is quietly guessed.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""agent-build-tools: GitHub-Issues-native ticket toolkit for agent-driven builds.
3	
4	Project-agnostic: swap languages/gates via the `tooling:` section of
5	build-plan/config.yaml (see config.example.yaml).
6	
7	A ticket IS a GitHub Issue — that is the single source of truth (open = to-do,
8	closed = done). There is no tasks.yaml and no sync step. This toolkit offloads
9	task selection, context assembly, verification, and the git/PR ceremony onto
10	deterministic commands so the model only has to write code.
11	
12	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py new "Title" ...   # create a correctly-formatted ticket issue
13	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py next               # id of the next runnable agent ticket
14	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py show T-012         # ticket body + its files + cited schema section
15	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py verify T-012       # run the ticket's Acceptance commands
16	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py start T-012        # flag the issue "In Progress" on the Project board
17	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py finish T-012       # verify, branch, commit, push, PR, merge, close (serial)
18	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py doctor [--fix]     # reconcile issues ↔ commits ↔ board ↔ branches
19	
20	Parallel execution (Model A — one orchestrator, N isolated worker worktrees):
21	
22	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py capacity                   # safe worker count from this machine's cores+RAM
23	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py batch --running A,B --max N # runnable tickets, file-disjoint from the in-flight set
24	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py worktree-add T-032         # make ../<repo>-worktrees/T-032 on branch task/T-032
25	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py submit T-032               # (in worktree) gate+build, add -A, commit, push, open PR
26	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py land T-032                 # (from main checkout) serialized squash-merge + cleanup
27	  python3 scripts/agent-tools.py worktree-rm T-032          # tear down a worker worktree
28	
29	Ticket data (milestone, depends-on, files, acceptance) is parsed from the issue
30	title + body; project-wide config (repo, project number, build frontier) lives
31	in build-plan/config.yaml. `submit` runs inside a worktree and is parallel-safe;
32	`land` serializes the merge to main behind a file lock and rebases-then-retries
33	on conflict.
34	
35	Board routing: a ticket's milestone default (a `projects:` map in config.yaml)
36	or $PROJECT_NUMBER / the global `project.project_number` decides which GitHub
37	Project its status updates target, so different phases can live on different boards.
38	"""
39	import os, re, sys, json, ast, subprocess, yaml, fcntl
40	
41	BUILD_PLAN = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
42	REPO = os.path.dirname(BUILD_PLAN)
43	# Project-type specifics (runnable commands, per-command cwd, build gates,
44	# test-path template) come from the `tooling:` section of build-plan/config.yaml.
45	WORKTREES = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(REPO), os.path.basename(REPO) + "-worktrees")
46	LOCKS = os.path.join(BUILD_PLAN, ".locks")
47	
48	
49	def sh(args, check=False, **kw):
50	    r = subprocess.run(args, text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=REPO, **kw)
51	    if check and r.returncode != 0:
52	        sys.exit(f"BLOCKED: `{' '.join(args)}` failed:\n{(r.stderr or r.stdout).strip()}")
53	    return r
54	
55	# ---- config + ticket loading (GitHub Issues = single source of truth) -------
56	_CONFIG = None
57	_TICKETS = None
58	
59	def config():
60	    """Project-wide settings from build-plan/config.yaml (never ticket data)."""
61	    global _CONFIG
62	    if _CONFIG is None:
63	        _CONFIG = yaml.safe_load(open(os.path.join(BUILD_PLAN, "config.yaml"))) or {}
64	    return _CONFIG
65	
66	def repo_slug():
67	    return config()["project"].get("repo") or sh(
68	        ["gh", "repo", "view", "--json", "nameWithOwner", "-q", ".nameWithOwner"]).stdout.strip()
69	
70	# ---- project-type tooling (config.yaml `tooling:`; defaults preserve the
71	# ---- original swift-project behavior so legacy configs keep working) --------
72	_DEFAULT_RUNNABLE = ("swift", "swiftlint", "xcodebuild", "python", "python3", "cd",
73	                     "bash", "sh", "kubectl", "kubeconform", "helm", "pytest",
74	                     "shellcheck", "make", "go", "npm", "cargo")
75	
76	def tooling():
77	    return config().get("tooling") or {}
78	
79	def runnable():
80	    return tuple(tooling().get("runnable") or _DEFAULT_RUNNABLE)
81	
82	def _cmd_cwd(c):
83	    """cwd for an acceptance command: first matching cwd_rule
84	    ({command: swift, dir: Packages/NifflerCore}), else the repo root."""
85	    head = c.split()[0]
86	    for rule in tooling().get("cwd_rules") or []:
87	        if head == rule.get("command"):
88	            p = os.path.join(REPO, rule.get("dir") or ".")
89	            if os.path.isdir(p):
90	                return p
91	    return REPO
92	
93	def _env2(name, default=None):
94	    """AGENT_<name> env var with legacy NIFFLER_<name> fallback."""
95	    return os.environ.get("AGENT_" + name) or os.environ.get("NIFFLER_" + name) or default
96	
97	def _ticket_id(title):
98	    m = re.match(r"\s*(T-\d+)", title or "")
99	    return m.group(1) if m else None
100	
101	def parse_issue(it):
102	    """Turn a GitHub issue (number,title,state,labels,milestone,body) into the
103	    task-dict shape the rest of the toolkit expects. The body header is the
104	    format `agent-tools.py new` (and the retired sync) emit, so it round-trips."""
105	    title = it.get("title", "")
106	    tid = _ticket_id(title)
107	    name = title.split("·", 1)[1].strip() if "·" in title else title
108	    labels = [l["name"] if isinstance(l, dict) else l for l in (it.get("labels") or [])]
109	    ms = it.get("milestone")
110	    milestone = (ms or {}).get("title") if isinstance(ms, dict) else ms
111	    body = it.get("body") or ""
112	    deps = []
113	    md = re.search(r"\*\*Depends on:\*\*\s*([^|\n]*)", body)
114	    if md:
115	        deps = re.findall(r"T-\d+", md.group(1))
116	    files = {"create": [], "modify": []}
117	    mf = re.search(r"\*\*Files\*\*.*?create:\s*(\[[^\]]*\])\s*;\s*modify:\s*(\[[^\]]*\])", body, re.S)
118	    if mf:
119	        for kind, grp in (("create", mf.group(1)), ("modify", mf.group(2))):
120	            try:
121	                files[kind] = list(ast.literal_eval(grp))
122	            except Exception:
123	                files[kind] = []
124	    parts = re.split(r"(?m)^---\s*$", body, maxsplit=1)
125	    md_body = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else body
126	    return {
127	        "id": tid, "title": name, "labels": labels,
128	        "assignee": "agent" if "agent" in labels else ("human" if "human" in labels else "agent"),
129	        "milestone": milestone, "depends_on": deps, "files": files,
130	        "body": md_body, "status": (it.get("state") or "").lower(), "number": it.get("number"),
131	    }
132	
133	def tickets():
134	    """All ticket issues, parsed, cached for the process. Issues without a T-id
135	    title prefix are ignored (they are not build tickets)."""
136	    global _TICKETS
137	    if _TICKETS is None:
138	        out = sh(["gh", "issue", "list", "--repo", repo_slug(), "--state", "all",
139	                  "--limit", "1000", "--json", "number,title,state,labels,milestone,body"])
140	        if out.returncode != 0:
141	            sys.exit(f"BLOCKED: cannot read GitHub issues (gh auth / network?):\n{out.stderr.strip()}")
142	        try:
143	            raw = json.loads(out.stdout or "[]")
144	        except Exception:
145	            raw = []
146	        _TICKETS = [parse_issue(it) for it in raw if _ticket_id(it.get("title", ""))]
147	    return _TICKETS
148	
149	def load():
150	    """Compatibility shim: a cfg dict shaped like the old tasks.yaml
151	    (project / projects / tasks), but tickets come from GitHub Issues."""
152	    c = dict(config())
153	    c["tasks"] = tickets()
154	    return c
155	
156	def by_id(cfg):
157	    # later issues win on duplicate ids (e.g. historical T-160 collisions); both
158	    # are closed so selection is unaffected.
159	    return {t["id"]: t for t in cfg["tasks"] if t["id"]}
160	
161	# ---- Project board status (best-effort; never blocks the build) ------------
162	def _json(r):
163	    try:
164	        return json.loads(r.stdout or "null")
165	    except Exception:
166	        return None
167	
168	def project_number_for(tid):
169	    """Which GitHub Project board this ticket belongs to. Resolution order:
170	    the ticket's own `project_number`, then its milestone default (a
171	    `projects:` map in tasks.yaml keyed by milestone id), then $PROJECT_NUMBER,
172	    then the global `project.project_number`. Lets phases live on separate boards."""
173	    cfg = load(); t = by_id(cfg).get(tid) or {}
174	    if t.get("project_number"):
175	        return str(t["project_number"])
176	    pmap = cfg.get("projects") or {}
177	    ms = (t.get("milestone") or "").split(" ", 1)[0].split("·")[0].strip()
178	    if ms and pmap.get(ms):
179	        return str(pmap[ms])
180	    return os.environ.get("PROJECT_NUMBER") or str(cfg["project"].get("project_number") or "")
181	
182	def _project(owner, num):
183	    """(project_node_id, number) for Project `num`, or (None, None)."""
184	    if not num:
185	        return (None, None)
186	    v = _json(sh(["gh", "project", "view", num, "--owner", owner, "--format", "json"]))
187	    return ((v or {}).get("id"), num)

189	def set_status(slug, tid, option, force=False):
190	    """Set the issue's Project Status field to `option` (e.g. 'In Progress', 'Done').
191	
192	    OPT-IN: each call costs several GraphQL queries (project view + field-list +
193	    item-list), which drains the GitHub API quota fast under an autonomous loop.
194	    The build doesn't need it — issue open/closed state is the source of truth,
195	    and GitHub's built-in "item closed → Done" Project workflow covers the column.
196	    Enable with $NIFFLER_BOARD=1 or project.board_status: true in config.yaml.
197	    `doctor --fix` passes force=True to reconcile the board regardless."""
198	    if not (force or _env2("BOARD") or config()["project"].get("board_status")):
199	        return
200	    owner = slug.split("/")[0]
201	    pid, num = _project(owner, project_number_for(tid))
202	    if not pid:
203	        print(f"(status: no project for {tid} — skipping '{option}'. Set project_number in tasks.yaml or export PROJECT_NUMBER.)")
204	        return

# ollama-code-mcp

An [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that lets Claude Code delegate
coding tasks to a local (or LAN) [Ollama](https://ollama.com) instance running
a Qwen3 model. Point it at a GPU box on your network -- a Tesla V100 running
`qwen3-coder:30b`, for example -- and Claude Code can hand off boilerplate
generation, test writing, diff review, and batch refactors to it instead of
spending cloud tokens and context window on them.

See [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md) for the routing guidance Claude Code reads to
decide what to delegate versus what to keep in the cloud.

## Why

- **Saves Claude's context window.** The file-aware tool variants take a
  `file_path` (or `diff_file`, or a `glob_pattern` for batches) and read the
  content server-side, so Claude never has to paste large files into a tool
  call just to hand them off.
- **Uses idle GPU capacity.** If you already run Ollama on a home GPU box or
  in a k3s cluster, this turns that capacity into a first-class Claude Code
  tool instead of a chat window you have to copy-paste into.
- **Fails safe.** If Ollama is unreachable, times out, or the model isn't
  pulled, tools return a clear, non-fatal message telling Claude to just
  handle the task itself rather than getting stuck retrying.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose | Inputs |
|---|---|---|
| `generate_code` | Generate new code from an instruction | `instruction`, `language`, `context_file` |
| `review_code` | Review code for bugs, security issues, simplifications | `code` or `file_path`, `focus` |
| `refactor_code` | Refactor code per an instruction, behavior-preserving | `instruction`, `code` or `file_path` |
| `fix_code` | Diagnose and fix a bug | `code` or `file_path`, `error_message` |
| `write_tests` | Write tests for given code | `code` or `file_path`, `framework` |
| `explain_code` | Explain what code does | `code` or `file_path` |
| `code_review_diff` | Review a git diff, PR-review style | `diff` or `diff_file`, `context` |
| `batch_refactor` | Apply an instruction across files matching a glob, sequentially | `glob_pattern`, `instruction`, `root_dir`, `dry_run` |
| `ollama_status` | Health check: reachability, configured model, available models | -- |

Every tool (except `ollama_status`) accepts a `think: bool` parameter. This
toggles Qwen3's extended reasoning by appending `/think` or `/no_think` to
the prompt (see [Think mode](#think-mode) below). All coding tools default to
`think=True`; `explain_code` defaults to `False` since explanations are
usually fast enough without it.

`code` / `file_path` (and `diff` / `diff_file`) pairs are mutually exclusive
-- pass exactly one. File paths are resolved and confined to
`OLLAMA_MCP_ALLOWED_DIR` (see [Configuration](#configuration)); attempts to
read or write outside it are rejected.

`refactor_code` returns the refactored code as text -- it does not touch
disk. `batch_refactor` is the one tool that can write files, and only when
called with `dry_run=False`; by default it returns a unified diff per file
so you can review before applying.

## Installation

Requires Python 3.10+.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:darthzen/ollama-code-mcp.git
cd ollama-code-mcp
pip install -e .
```

Or with `uv`:

```bash
uv pip install -e .
```

### Register with Claude Code

Add to your Claude Code MCP config (`claude mcp add` or the `mcpServers`
block in your settings), pointing `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` at wherever Ollama
actually listens -- commonly a LAN address, not localhost, since the model
runs on a dedicated GPU host:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ollama-code": {
      "command": "ollama-code-mcp",
      "env": {
        "OLLAMA_BASE_URL": "http://ollama.ash4d.com:11434",
        "OLLAMA_MODEL": "qwen3-coder:30b",
        "OLLAMA_MCP_ALLOWED_DIR": "/Users/you/code"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Or run it straight from the repo without installing:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ollama-code": {
      "command": "/path/to/ollama-code-mcp/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "ollama_code_mcp.server"],
      "env": { "OLLAMA_BASE_URL": "http://ollama.ash4d.com:11434" }
    }
  }
}
```

`OLLAMA_MCP_ALLOWED_DIR` should be set to the project root (or a parent of
every project) you want file-aware tools to be able to read/write. It
defaults to the server's current working directory.

## Configuration

All configuration is via environment variables:

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:11434` | Where Ollama listens. LAN addresses and bare `host:port` (scheme added automatically) are supported. |
| `OLLAMA_MODEL` | `qwen3-coder` | Model tag to use, as shown by `ollama list` on the target host. |
| `OLLAMA_TIMEOUT` | `900` | Request timeout in seconds. Defaults to 15 minutes to allow large generations/refactors on modest hardware. |

Every one of the six tools:

assertion is the whole safety model in one line — do not weaken it.

implement:

* an `effect` string that enumerates **every** rule change as a diff, one line

pass the caller's value through **verbatim** and never synthesise one.

| `nv_trigger_bench_run` | `POST /v1/bench/host/{id}/kubernetes`, `.../docker` | `False` |

### `runtime_ops`

| Tool | Endpoint | `destructiveHint` |
|---|---|---|
| `nv_quarantine_workload` | `POST /v1/workload/request/{id}` | `True` |
| `nv_set_service_mode` | `PATCH /v1/service/config`, `/network`, `/profile` | `False` |
| `nv_start_packet_capture` | `POST /v1/sniffer` | `False` |
| `nv_stop_packet_capture` | `PATCH /v1/sniffer/stop/{id}` | `False` |

## Secret handling — the two-payload rule

Registry credentials pass through three of these tools. Part D section D.0
defines the normative mechanism and you must implement it exactly:

```
wire_payload  = the real body, with real credentials  -> client.request() ONLY
safe_payload  = redact_secrets(wire_payload)          -> the guard AND WriteOutcome.payload
confirm_token = sha256(op | target | canonical_json(safe_payload))[:12]
```

The token is computed over the **redacted** payload so that preview and execution
agree. The deliberate consequence, stated in Part D: changing only the secret does
not invalidate the token. That is accepted; document it in a comment so nobody
"fixes" it later and breaks the handshake.

`controller_response` is redacted for every tool in this phase.

## Asynchronous scans

`nv_trigger_scan` returns as soon as the controller accepts the request. It does
not wait and it must not poll. Its docstring tells the caller to read progress via
`nv_get_scan_status` (Phase 3). Use `settings.long_request_timeout_s` for the
request itself.

`nv_scan_repository` is the exception: it is synchronous, slow, and returns a full
report. Project and cap it exactly like `nv_get_scan_report`. Drop
`RESTScanRepoReport.envs` and `labels` — environment variables carry credentials.

## Packet capture

`GET /v1/sniffer/{id}/pcap` is **deliberately not exposed**. A binary pcap is not
a sane MCP result. `nv_start_packet_capture`'s docstring says so and tells the
operator to retrieve the capture out of band. Capture is privacy-sensitive; the
`effect` string must name the target workload and the filter.

## Quarantine

`nv_quarantine_workload` severs a running container's network. `destructiveHint=True`,
and the `effect` string says the container will lose network connectivity
immediately. The same endpoint un-quarantines; Part D names the exact field.

and confirmed-applies with the exact body. Plus:

* `test_update_registry_password_not_logged`

The secret-not-logged tests must use `capfd`, because structlog binds stderr with
`cache_logger_on_first_use=True` — `caplog` will not see the output. Part D
explains this.

## Goal

Two new files: `src/neuvector_mcp/tools/iam.py` (4 read + 5 write tools) and
`src/neuvector_mcp/tools/system.py` (3 write tools), both registered in
`server.py`.

`tools/iam.py` registers **two** toolsets from one module. Its `register()`
therefore has two independent `if settings.toolset_enabled(...)` guards, not one.
Read tools go under `iam_read`, write tools under `iam_write`. A read tool tagged
`iam_write` fails gate rule R3.

## Tools

### `iam_read` (4)

| `nv_update_user_role` | `PATCH /v1/user/{fullname}/role/{role}` | `False` |

### `system_write` (3)

| Tool | Endpoint | `destructiveHint` |

| `nv_set_namespace_tags` | `PATCH /v1/domain/{name}` | `False` |
| `nv_update_scan_config` | `PATCH /v1/scan/config` | `False` |

## Secret handling — three distinct rules

| Secret | Rule |
|---|---|
| `RESTUser.password` on create | Two-payload rule from Phase 9: real value on the wire, `"***"` in the preview payload and in `WriteOutcome.payload`, token computed over the redacted form. **Never** projected on read. |
| `RESTApikey.apikey_secret` on create | **Returned to the caller** — that is the point of the tool, and the controller shows it once. Never logged; the audit record notes only that a key was created. Never retrievable afterwards, so `nv_list_api_keys` cannot and must not return it. |
| Auth server bind passwords and client secrets | `nv_list_auth_servers` uses an **allowlist** projection: only the fields Part B names are read by value; every other key is reported by name only, with name-matches on `password`/`secret`/`token`/`credential`/`private`/`key` diverted to a `redacted_keys` list. An allowlist, not a denylist — a controller upgrade that adds a secret field must fail closed. |

## `nv_update_system_config` — the one sanctioned pre-guard read

This tool performs a **read-only, failure-tolerant** `GET /v2/system/config`
before calling the guard, so its `effect` string can name each field as
`old -> new`. Part D section D.0.8 bounds this exception:

* the GET is the only network call permitted before the guard,
* a failure of that GET must not fail the tool — fall back to naming the new
  values only,
* the PATCH still happens only after confirmation.

`test_update_system_config_preview_reads_current_config_only` asserts exactly one
GET and zero PATCHes on the preview call. That test is what keeps this exception
from becoming a loophole.

Enumerate the highest-risk sub-fields in the docstring: cluster-wide enforcement
defaults, syslog destination, webhooks, and network settings.

## `nv_update_user_role`

Part D justifies choosing `PATCH /v1/user/{fullname}/role/{role}` over
`PATCH /v1/user/{fullname}`: the role travels in a verified path, and it avoids
sharing a request body with `password` and `email`. Keep that reasoning as a
comment.

**Base image policy: openSUSE or SUSE BCI only.** The Dockerfile uses

-# agent-build-tools config for the NeuVector MCP server build.
# Tickets are GitHub Issues (open = to-do, closed = done); this file holds
# project-wide config only, never ticket data.
project:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  repo: "darthzen/neuvector-mcp"
  build_through: M11       # highest milestone agents may build ($BUILD_THROUGH overrides)
  board_status: false      # milestones only; issue state is the source of truth
projects: {}

tooling:
  # Acceptance commands must start with one of these to be executed by verify/finish.
  # Everything runs through `make ... PY=.venv/bin/python` so the gate always uses
  # the project venv rather than whatever python3 the shell happens to resolve.
  runnable: [make, python3, python, bash, sh, pytest, kubectl, podman, cd]
  cwd_rules: []            # every command runs at the repo root
  # Tests live in tests/<name>.py; the toolkit auto-stages files named by a
  # `--filter <Name>` in the body (harmless here, we list files explicitly).
  test_path_template: "tests/{name}.py"
  # `show` pulls cited §N sections out of this doc into the ticket context.
  schema_doc: SPEC.md
  # Acceptance line for `new` when no body is given.
  default_acceptance: "make verify PY=.venv/bin/python"

# Session provenance: `entire enable` has already been run in this repo, so
# re-anchor the farming session onto the squash commit after each merge.
entire:
  enabled: true
  agent: claude-code
  amend: false

import subprocess

invention is the failure mode this spec is shaped to prevent:

{reading}
"""

DOD = """## Definition of done
`make verify` exits 0, the tool count is exactly as stated, the change is limited
to the files listed above, and the commit is `[{tid}] <title>` closing this issue.
"""


def body(tid, context, reading, deps, create, modify, steps, acceptance,
         guardrails, extra=""):
    dep_lines = "\n".join(f"- {d} (must be closed first)" for d in deps) or "- none"
    c = "\n".join(f"- `{f}`" for f in create) or "- (none)"
    m = "\n".join(f"- `{f}`" for f in modify) or "- (none)"
    acc = "\n".join(f"- [ ] {a}" for a in acceptance)
    steps_md = "\n".join(f"{i}. {s}" for i, s in enumerate(steps, 1))
    g = "\n".join(f"- {x}" for x in guardrails)
    return f"""## Context
{context}

{READING_PREAMBLE.format(reading=reading)}
## Dependencies
{dep_lines}

## Files
Create:
{c}
Modify:
{m}
Do NOT touch anything else.

## Steps
{steps_md}
{extra}
## Acceptance
Runnable checks. The task is done only when all pass.
{acc}

## Out of scope / guardrails
{g}

{DOD.format(tid=tid)}"""

# ---- read-tool ticket helper ---------------------------------------------
def read_tools_ticket(tid, milestone, area, depends, title, tools, count,
                      part, part_section, module, testfile, fixtures,
                      new_module, context, hard, extra_reading="", extra_guards=()):
    tool_list = "\n".join(f"   - `{n}` — `{ep}`" for n, ep in tools)
    create, modify = [], ["src/neuvector_mcp/models.py"]
    (create if new_module else modify).append(module)
    (create if new_module else modify).append(testfile)
    if new_module:
        modify.append("src/neuvector_mcp/server.py")
    create += [f"tests/fixtures/{f}" for f in fixtures]
    steps = [
        "Append the new output models to the end of `models.py`, in the order the Part "
        "file lists them. Nothing above them changes.",
        "Write the fixtures named above. Every field name comes from "
        f"`{APPB}` — do not invent one. Every list fixture must hold more items than "
        "the smallest `limit` its test uses, so the over-fetch-by-one truncation path "
        "is actually exercised.",
        ("Create " if new_module else "Extend ") + f"`{module}` with these tools, each "
        "one exactly as the Part file specifies its arguments, query mapping, verbatim "
        "docstring, output model `from_api()` and envelope key:\n" + tool_list,
    ]
    if new_module:
        steps.append("Register the module in `server.py`'s `TOOL_MODULES` list.")
    steps += [
        f"{'Create' if new_module else 'Extend'} `{testfile}` with the test functions "
        f"the Part file names per tool. {TESTS_NOTE}",
        "Run the gate and report the exact tool count from `make spec`.",
    ]
    reading = (
        f"1. `SPEC.md` sections 3, 7.3, 7.5, 7.6, 12\n"
        f"2. `{PHASE}/{milestone_phase(milestone)}`\n"
        f"3. `{part}` — section {part_section}\n"
        f"4. `{APPB}` for every field you touch{extra_reading}"
    )
    add(tid=tid, milestone=milestone, area=area, assignee="agent", depends=depends,
        title=title, create=create, modify=modify, context=context, reading=reading,
        steps=steps,
        acceptance=[f"`{GATE}`", f"`{count_check(count)}`"],
        guardrails=list(READ_TOOL_GUARDS) + list(extra_guards),
        extra=("\n## The hard part\n" + hard + "\n") if hard else "")

# ---- write-tool ticket helper --------------------------------------------
def write_tools_ticket(tid, milestone, area, depends, title, tools, count,
                       part, part_section, module, testfile, fixtures,
                       new_module, context, hard, extra_reading="",
                       extra_guards=(), models=True):
    tool_list = "\n".join(f"   - `{n}` — `{ep}` — `destructiveHint={d}`"
                          for n, ep, d in tools)
    create, modify = [], (["src/neuvector_mcp/models.py"] if models else [])
    (create if new_module else modify).append(module)
    (create if new_module else modify).append(testfile)
    if new_module:
        modify.append("src/neuvector_mcp/server.py")
    create += [f"tests/fixtures/{f}" for f in fixtures]
    steps = []
    if models:
        steps.append(
            "Append the input models Part C/D specifies to the end of `models.py`, in "
            "the order the Part file lists them. Nothing above them changes.")
    if fixtures:
        steps.append(
            "Write the fixtures named above; every field name comes from "
            f"`{APPB}`. Most write endpoints return an empty body — stub those routes "
            "with `json={}` rather than inventing a fixture.")
    steps.append(
        ("Create " if new_module else "Extend ") + f"`{module}` with these tools, each "
        "one following the five-step mutating-tool body from SPEC.md 7.4 exactly:\n"
        + tool_list)
    if new_module:
        steps.append("Register the module in `server.py`'s `TOOL_MODULES` list.")
    steps += [
        f"{'Create' if new_module else 'Extend'} `{testfile}` with, at minimum per "
        "tool, `test_<tool>_preview_sends_nothing` (asserting "
        "`route.call_count == 0`) and `test_<tool>_confirmed_applies` (asserting the "
        f"**exact** JSON body and `call_count == 1`). {TESTS_NOTE}",
        "Run the gate and report the exact tool count from `make spec`.",
    ]
    reading = (
        f"1. `SPEC.md` sections 6 (safety model), 7.4 (the five-step body), 12 (gate rules)\n"
        f"2. `{PHASE}/{milestone_phase(milestone)}`\n"
        f"3. `{part}` — section {part_section}\n"
        f"4. `{APPB}` and `{APPC}`\n"
        f"5. `tests/test_guard.py` — the tests that already pin the handshake{extra_reading}"
    )
    add(tid=tid, milestone=milestone, area=area, assignee="agent", depends=depends,
        title=title, create=create, modify=modify, context=context, reading=reading,
        steps=steps,
        acceptance=[f"`{GATE}`", f"`{count_check(count)}`"],
        guardrails=list(WRITE_TOOL_GUARDS) + list(extra_guards),
        extra=("\n## The hard part\n" + hard + "\n") if hard else "")

Done. `github.com/darthzen/neuvector-mcp` is live with a 34-issue queue.

## What's there

**Repo** — public, spec package committed, `agent-build-tools` as a submodule at `build-plan/tools`, config at `build-plan/config.yaml` (repo slug, `build_through: M11`, milestones-only, `entire:` re-anchoring enabled since you'd already run `entire enable`).

**12 milestones** M0–M11, one per spec phase. **34 tickets**, issues #1–#34, all round-tripped back through the toolkit's own parser — deps, file lists and acceptance commands all parse.

The chunking unit is a *coherent tool group*, not a phase, because `verify_spec` R8 fails any tool with no test and coverage gates at 85% — so models + fixtures + tool + tests have to land in one commit. Every ticket gates on:

```
make verify PY=.venv/bin/python
make spec  PY=.venv/bin/python | grep -q "N tools introspected"
```

with N walking 5 → 9 → 13 → 16 → 19 → 20 → … → 72, so a miscount fails the build rather than being reported as "looks right". T-030 additionally gates the 41-tool read-only surface. Each body carries the exact reading list (`§`-cited so `show` injects the SPEC sections automatically), the named test functions, the endpoint/envelope traps (`summarys`, `process_profile_config`, the per-event-kind filter tags, `PATCH /v1/admission/rule` having no `{id}`), and BLOCKED-not-invent guardrails.

The three highest-blast-radius tools each got their own ticket: `nv_get_scan_report` (#9), `nv_apply_network_rule_changes` (#18), `nv_set_admission_state` (#21).

## Running it

```bash
cd ~/Developer/neuvector-mcp
python3 build-plan/tools/agent-tools.py next     # → T-001
python3 build-plan/tools/agent-tools.py show T-001   # body + files + cited SPEC §§
# delegate the code to qwen3-coder:30b via ollama-code
python3 build-plan/tools/agent-tools.py finish T-001 # verify, branch, PR, squash-merge, close
```

`ollama_status` confirms the GPU box at `192.168.7.160:9401` is up with `qwen3-coder:30b` — the model this spec was written for.

## Two things to know

**The queue is serial by design.** Every ticket appends to `models.py`, its toolset module and `server.py`, so the worktree/`batch`/`land` parallel flow won't help here — `capacity` would hand you file-conflicting work. Use `next` → `finish`.

**Python risk at T-001.** `pyenv` only offers 3.11.9 (below the `requires-python = ">=3.12"` floor) and 3.14.5, so the venv will be built on 3.14 against pins written for 3.12/3.13 — `fastmcp==3.4.5`, `pydantic==2.13.4`, `mypy==1.18.2`. The ticket forbids bumping those pins and tells the agent to report BLOCKED with the pip output instead, so if a wheel is missing you'll get a clean stop rather than a silent dependency drift. Installing a 3.13 via pyenv first would sidestep it.

M11 has two `human` tickets — #32 (cluster dry-run, needs secrets) and #33 (live smoke test, needs a controller). The toolkit never picks those up; #34 depends on #31 rather than on them, so the agent queue runs uninterrupted to the end.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Create the GitHub Project (v2) board for this build and put all 34 tickets on
# it, then point build-plan/config.yaml at it.

# Run from the repo root:  bash build-plan/create-board.sh
set -euo pipefail

TITLE="NeuVector MCP"

NUM=$(gh project create --owner "$OWNER" --title "$TITLE" --format json \
      | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["number"])')
echo "    project number: $NUM"

echo "==> adding 34 tickets"
gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state all --limit 100 --json url --jq '.[].url' \
  | sort -t/ -k7 -n \
  | while read -r url; do
      gh project item-add "$NUM" --owner "$OWNER" --url "$url" >/dev/null
      echo "    + $url"
    done

echo "==> wiring build-plan/config.yaml"
python3 - "$NUM" <<'PY'
import re, sys
num = sys.argv[1]
p = "build-plan/config.yaml"
s = open(p).read()

              f"  project_number: {num}        # GitHub Project (v2) board\n  build_through: M11")
s = re.sub(r"  board_status: false.*", "  board_status: true       # push Status to the board on start/finish", s)
open(p, "w").write(s)
print(open(p).read())
PY

content.text:
Short answer: **Entire will capture the work, but it won't distinguish qwen from Claude.** Here's why, from the CLI rather than from memory.

## What Entire's attribution unit actually is

`entire agent list` on this repo:

```
✓ claude-code
  codex  copilot-cli  cursor  factoryai-droid  gemini  opencode  pi
```

Attribution is per **agent CLI session**, established by hooks that agent installs. There is no ollama or qwen integration, and there can't be one here — qwen3-coder:30b isn't a session, it's an MCP tool (`mcp__ollama-code__*`) called *from inside* the Claude Code session. The session record has exactly one model field:

```json
{ "agent": "Claude Code", "model": "claude-opus-5",
  "tokens": { "total": 5859611, "cache_read": 5626966, ... },
  "files_touched": [...] }
```

Those 5.8M tokens are Claude's alone — qwen's tokens are spent on your GPU box and never reach Entire. So each merged ticket will land as one checkpoint, correctly re-anchored onto the squash commit by `finish` (that's the `entire:` block doing its job), labelled Claude Code / claude-opus-5. The diff will contain qwen's code with Claude's name on it.

## Why it can't infer it either

The commit is built by `agent-tools.py:477`:

```python
sh(["git", "commit", "-m", f"[{tid}] {t['title']}{closes}"], check=True)
```

`[T-009] vulnerability: nv_get_scan_report…` + `Closes #9`. No model provenance anywhere, and the PR body (line 482) is just the same `Closes #n`. Nothing downstream of the tool call records which model produced the text.

## Getting real attribution

Three options, cheapest first:

**1. PR-body trailer (recommended).** `submit` already proves the pattern — it writes `Entire-Session: <sid>` into the PR body so `land` can read it back after the merge. A `Generated-By: qwen3-coder:30b (ollama-code-mcp)` line alongside it survives the squash, because GitHub builds the squash commit message from the PR title and body. That makes it greppable in `git log` on `main` forever, and visible in the Entire checkpoint since checkpoints are tied to commits. Needs a small patch to `agent-build-tools` — which would also benefit Niffler and nemoclaw-ops-agent.

**2. `Co-Authored-By:` trailer.** Same mechanism, but GitHub renders it as a co-author avatar on the commit. Slightly abusive of the field (qwen isn't a GitHub user), and it'll show as an unlinked author.

**3. Issue comment per ticket, no tooling change.** Before `finish`, comment on the issue with which model generated what and which `ollama-code` tools were called. Zero code change, but it lives in GitHub only — not in `git log`, not in the Entire checkpoint.

There's also an honest limit worth naming: none of these captures *how much* of a ticket was qwen's. If I hand qwen a `generate_code` call and then rewrite half the output before writing the file, a flat `Generated-By:` overstates it. If you want that granularity it has to be per-file or per-hunk, which none of this tooling does today.

Want me to patch `agent-build-tools` for option 1? It's a contained change — a `provenance:` block in `config.yaml` and a trailer appended in `cmd_finish`/`cmd_submit` — and I'd send it as a PR to that repo rather than editing the submodule in place.
Let's patch for option 1.

def _pr_body(slug, branch):
    r = sh(["gh", "pr", "view", branch, "--repo", slug, "--json", "body", "-q", ".body"])
    return r.stdout if r.returncode == 0 else ""

# ---- model provenance seam (opt-in via config `provenance:`) ---------------
# Entire attributes work to an agent *session* (claude-code, codex, cursor, …).
# When that session delegates code generation to another model — e.g. Claude Code
# handing a ticket to qwen3-coder:30b over ollama-code-mcp — the delegate is an
# MCP tool call inside the session, not a session of its own: it installs no
# hooks, spends no tokens Entire can see, and gets no attribution. The checkpoint
# reads as pure claude-code work even though another model wrote the diff.
#
# This seam records the writing model as a `Generated-By:` trailer. Omit the
# `provenance:` config block entirely (the default) and nothing changes.
PROVENANCE_MARKER = "Generated-By:"

def provenance_cfg():
    return config().get("provenance") or {}

def provenance_on():
    return bool(provenance_cfg().get("enabled"))

def generated_by():
    """The model that wrote this ticket's code, or None when unset/disabled.
    $AGENT_GENERATED_BY overrides the config value so a single worker can record
    a per-run model without editing config.yaml."""
    if not provenance_on():
        return None
    return (_env2("GENERATED_BY") or provenance_cfg().get("generated_by") or "").strip() or None

def provenance_trailer():
    """`Generated-By: <model>` for the commit message AND the PR body.

    It has to go in the PR body, not just the branch commit: finish/land
    squash-merge through `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`, and GitHub builds
    the squash commit message from the PR title and body. A trailer that lives
    only on the branch commit is deleted with the branch and never reaches main —
    the same failure that orphans Entire checkpoints (see ENTIRE_MARKER above)."""
    m = generated_by()
    return f"\n\n{PROVENANCE_MARKER} {m}" if m else ""

def generated_by_from_body(body):
    """Read the trailer back out of a PR body or commit message."""
    m = re.search(rf"(?m)^{re.escape(PROVENANCE_MARKER)}\s*(.+?)\s*$", body or "")
    return m.group(1) if m else None

## Model provenance (`Generated-By:`)

Entire — and git — attribute a ticket to the **agent session** that ran it. When
that session delegates the actual code generation to another model, the delegate
gets no attribution: an [ollama-code-mcp](https://github.com/darthzen/ollama-code-mcp)
call handing a ticket to `qwen3-coder:30b` is a tool call *inside* the Claude Code
session, so it installs no hooks, spends no tokens Entire can see, and the
checkpoint reads as pure `claude-code` work even though another model wrote the
diff.

Enable the opt-in `provenance:` block and `finish`/`submit` record the writing
model as a trailer:

```yaml
provenance:
  enabled: true
  generated_by: "qwen3-coder:30b (ollama-code-mcp)"
```

```
[T-009] vulnerability: nv_get_scan_report with client-side severity filter

Closes #9

Generated-By: qwen3-coder:30b (ollama-code-mcp)
```

The trailer goes on the branch commit **and** in the PR body. The body is the
part that matters: `gh pr merge --squash` builds a new commit message from the PR
title and body, so a trailer that lives only on the branch commit dies with the
branch — the same way an un-re-anchored Entire checkpoint does. Because it lands
on `main`, it is greppable forever (`git log --grep '^Generated-By:'`) and it
shows up in the Entire checkpoint, since checkpoints are tied to commits.

`$AGENT_GENERATED_BY` overrides `generated_by` for one run, so a fleet of workers
on different models can each record their own without touching `config.yaml`.
Omit the block and the toolkit stays provenance-unaware.

**What this does not give you:** it is per *ticket*, not per file or per hunk. If
the driving agent rewrites half of what the delegate returned, a flat
`Generated-By:` overstates the delegate's share. Treat it as "this model was in
the loop for this ticket", not as a measured contribution.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests for the model-provenance seam (`Generated-By:`) in agent-tools.py.

Self-contained: no pytest required (`python3 tests/test_provenance_seam.py`), but
the test_* functions are also collectable by pytest. Nothing here touches git,
GitHub or Ollama — the seam is pure string construction plus config/env gating,
which is exactly what makes it safe to assert deterministically.
"""
import importlib.util, os, sys

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_SCRIPT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(_HERE), "agent-tools.py")


def _load_module():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("agent_tools", _SCRIPT)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


mod = _load_module()


def _configure(provenance=None):
    """Inject a config dict (bypasses reading config.yaml)."""
    cfg = {"project": {"repo": "owner/repo"}}
    if provenance is not None:
        cfg["provenance"] = provenance
    mod._CONFIG = cfg


def _clear_env():
    for k in ("AGENT_GENERATED_BY", "NIFFLER_GENERATED_BY"):
        os.environ.pop(k, None)


# ---- gating ---------------------------------------------------------------
def test_disabled_by_default():
    _clear_env(); _configure(provenance=None)
    assert mod.provenance_on() is False
    assert mod.generated_by() is None
    assert mod.provenance_trailer() == "", "absent config block must add nothing"

def test_explicitly_disabled_adds_nothing():
    _clear_env()
    _configure(provenance={"enabled": False, "generated_by": "qwen3-coder:30b"})
    assert mod.provenance_trailer() == ""

def test_enabled_without_model_adds_nothing():
    """enabled: true with no model is a misconfiguration, not a reason to emit
    an empty trailer that would land a bare `Generated-By:` line on main."""
    _clear_env(); _configure(provenance={"enabled": True})
    assert mod.generated_by() is None
    assert mod.provenance_trailer() == ""

def test_blank_model_is_treated_as_unset():
    _clear_env(); _configure(provenance={"enabled": True, "generated_by": "   "})
    assert mod.generated_by() is None
    assert mod.provenance_trailer() == ""


# ---- trailer construction -------------------------------------------------
def test_trailer_shape():
    _clear_env()
    _configure(provenance={"enabled": True, "generated_by": "qwen3-coder:30b (ollama-code-mcp)"})
    tr = mod.provenance_trailer()
    assert tr.startswith("\n\n"), "trailer must be its own paragraph"
    assert tr.strip() == "Generated-By: qwen3-coder:30b (ollama-code-mcp)"

def test_trailer_survives_body_composition():
    """The trailer must remain a line-anchored trailer once appended to a real
    PR body, because that body becomes the squash commit message."""
    _clear_env()
    _configure(provenance={"enabled": True, "generated_by": "qwen3-coder:30b"})
    body = "Closes #9" + mod.provenance_trailer()
    assert "Closes #9" in body
    assert mod.generated_by_from_body(body) == "qwen3-coder:30b"

def test_coexists_with_entire_marker():
    """submit appends both trailers; neither may swallow the other."""
    _clear_env()
    mod._CONFIG = {"project": {"repo": "owner/repo"},
                   "provenance": {"enabled": True, "generated_by": "qwen3-coder:30b"},
                   "entire": {"enabled": True}}
    body = "Closes #9" + mod.provenance_trailer() + mod.entire_pr_marker("sess-42")
    assert mod.generated_by_from_body(body) == "qwen3-coder:30b"
    assert mod.entire_session_from_body(body) == "sess-42"


# ---- env override ---------------------------------------------------------
def test_env_overrides_config():
    _clear_env()
    _configure(provenance={"enabled": True, "generated_by": "from-config"})
    os.environ["AGENT_GENERATED_BY"] = "devstral2:24b"
    try:
        assert mod.generated_by() == "devstral2:24b"
    finally:
        _clear_env()

def test_env_does_not_enable_a_disabled_seam():
    """A stray env var must not start writing trailers into a repo that never
    opted in."""
    _clear_env(); _configure(provenance=None)
    os.environ["AGENT_GENERATED_BY"] = "devstral2:24b"
    try:
        assert mod.generated_by() is None
        assert mod.provenance_trailer() == ""
    finally:
        _clear_env()

def test_legacy_niffler_env_fallback():
    _clear_env(); _configure(provenance={"enabled": True})
    os.environ["NIFFLER_GENERATED_BY"] = "qwen3-coder:30b"
    try:
        assert mod.generated_by() == "qwen3-coder:30b"
    finally:
        _clear_env()


# ---- read-back ------------------------------------------------------------
def test_from_body_none_when_absent():
    assert mod.generated_by_from_body("Closes #5\n\nno trailer here") is None
    assert mod.generated_by_from_body("") is None
    assert mod.generated_by_from_body(None) is None

def test_from_body_ignores_inline_mention():
    """Only a line-anchored trailer counts — prose mentioning the marker must
    not be mistaken for provenance."""
    assert mod.generated_by_from_body("we discussed Generated-By: foo in review") is None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    tests = [v for k, v in sorted(globals().items()) if k.startswith("test_") and callable(v)]
    failed = 0
    for t in tests:
        try:
            t()
            print(f"PASS  {t.__name__}")
        except AssertionError as e:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL  {t.__name__}: {e}")
        except Exception as e:
            failed += 1
            print(f"ERROR {t.__name__}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    print(f"\n{len(tests) - failed}/{len(tests)} passed")
    sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

```

The trailer goes in the **PR body**, not just the branch commit — that's the load-bearing detail. `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` rebuilds the commit message from the PR title and body, so a branch-only trailer dies with the branch, exactly the way an un-re-anchored Entire checkpoint does. This is a classic recursive implementation of the Fibonacci sequence, but with a subtle issue that makes it inefficient and potentially problematic.

## What it does
The function calculates the nth Fibonacci number where F(0)=0, F(1)=1, and each subsequent number is the sum of the two preceding ones. It's a direct translation of the mathematical definition.

## Control and Data Flow
- **Base case**: When `n < 2`, it returns `n` directly (0 for n=0, 1 for n=1)
- **Recursive case**: For n≥2, it makes two recursive calls: `f(n-1)` and `f(n-2)`, then sums their results
- **Call tree**: This creates a binary tree of recursive calls that grows exponentially

## The Critical Problem
This implementation has **exponential time complexity O(2^n)** due to massive redundant calculations. For example, computing `f(5)` calculates `f(3)` multiple times, and `f(2)` even more so. Each call branches into two more calls, leading to an exponential explosion in the number of function calls.

## Edge Cases and Assumptions
- **No input validation**: It assumes `n` is a non-negative integer
- **Stack overflow risk**: For large `n`, this will cause a RecursionError
- **Performance**: Even moderate values like n=30 take seconds to compute
- **Memory usage**: Each recursive call consumes stack space, leading to O(n) space complexity

## Non-obvious behavior
The function is mathematically correct but practically unusable for n > 20. A proper implementation would use memoization, iteration, or matrix exponentiation to achieve O(n) or O(log n) time complexity.

This is often used as a teaching example to illustrate the pitfalls of naive recursion, but it's essentially a "naive" implementation that demonstrates why algorithmic complexity matters."}

```bash
claude mcp remove ollama-code -s user

I've deliberately not removed the local server yet. It's broken for default calls but still works with a per-call `model=` override, and swapping it for an unreachable endpoint would leave no farm-out path at all.

## 2. The in-cluster server cannot see your code

This is the one I'd want you to weigh before committing to the move:

```
volumeMounts: [{mountPath: /workspace, name: workspace}]
volumes:      [{name: workspace, emptyDir: {}}]
OLLAMA_MCP_ALLOWED_DIR: /workspace
```

`/workspace` is an **emptyDir** — an empty scratch volume inside the pod. The local server has `OLLAMA_MCP_ALLOWED_DIR=/Users/rashford/Developer`, so it reads the repo and the spec package straight off disk. The cluster one has access to nothing.

That disables every file-aware variant — `file_path`, `context_file`, `diff_file`, `glob_pattern`, `batch_refactor`. I'd have to read each spec section myself and paste it into `code=`/`instruction=`, which spends my context on exactly the payloads the README says those variants exist to avoid:

> the file-aware tool variants take a `file_path` … and read the content server-side, so Claude never has to paste large files into a tool call just to hand them off.

It bites hardest on this project specifically, because the tool contracts are big: the `Toolset policy_read` section of PART-B alone is ~900 lines, and every ticket needs one of those sections plus the current state of an evolving module.

Three ways out, roughly in order of effort:

1. **Back `/workspace` with a PVC and sync the spec package into it.** The spec is static, so a one-time copy covers the reading side; only the evolving `models.py` / toolset module would need refreshing per ticket. Survives pod restarts, unlike emptyDir.
2. **`kubectl cp` the spec package into the running pod.** Works today, zero infra change — but emptyDir dies with the pod, so it's re-do-it-every-restart.
3. **Keep the local stdio server for farming** and just correct its `OLLAMA_MODEL` to `qwen3.6:27b-q6-precise`. Preserves file-aware tools; loses the centralized config you're clearly moving toward.

Your call — and it's a real tradeoff, not a reason to abandon the move. Tell me when the IP lands and which of the three you want, and I'll wire it up and start T-001. In the meantime the trailer is corrected and pushed: `Generated-By: qwen3.6:27b-q6-precise (ollama-code-mcp)`.
